value.text: Acceptance now uses a shared process-group watchdog: the original 45-second deadline sends SIGTERM, then a separate five-second cleanup window sends SIGKILL. The deterministic negative control uses a real CPU-spinning child that ignores SIGTERM; the watchdog force-kills it with unchanged durable fixture bytes. This bounds the historical installed-host timeout without claiming the dangling-lock defect was its original cause or increasing the execution deadline. The CLI lock defect itself now honors its existing wait budget.
